PLANNING BRIEF

A plan is more than
a traffic number.

What needs your attention

Model assumptions & data sources +

Road and place locations are an OpenStreetMap snapshot. Event pins and access points are approximate. Traffic counts, road capacities, speed assumptions and parking capacities are synthetic. This prototype is not a calibrated forecast, navigation service or emergency-access certification.

Road closures remove complete OSM way segments, respecting mapped one-way directions. Four approach nodes are snapped to the nearest connected major-road nodes in the baseline network. Their routes distribute event cars equally to the nearest major-road node at the venue. We calculate a first-pass assignment, then travel times using a BPR-style curve; this is not a traffic equilibrium or queue simulation. Existing background traffic is not rerouted. Unreachable approaches are flagged; the remaining-route average is not a full-trip estimate.

Cars = (car passengers − shuttle passengers) ÷ car occupancy. Each shuttle carries 40 passengers on two trips; shuttle movements are added to road demand. Arrivals use a normalized half-hour profile over 1–3 hours. Departures span two hours after the event. Peak parking assumes 85% of arriving cars remain parked. The timeline conserves arriving and departing cars. Emergency estimates follow mapped roads from a nearby connected road node at GMSH Sector-16 to the nearest major-road venue node, with two minutes of assumed access time. Routes outside the downloaded study area are not evaluated.

Scenario A uses the original inputs and open roads. Scenario B uses the same event plus closures, shuttles, extra parking and an extended arrival window. Date and start time set timeline labels; they do not change background traffic. All generated reports include these limitations.

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL · Leaflet map library. No live traffic feed is connected.
